- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimates later days.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 50+), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overestimates persist for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert toward historical averages too early, missing sustained upward trends.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of true values, especially in the last 10–15 days — model fails to capture late-stage price momentum.
- Model underestimates true values when recent history includes high volatility or sharp upward moves — fails to adjust for momentum.
- Model tends to underestimate true values when the last 5–10 days show strong upward trends — fails to recognize continuation or acceleration.
- Model overestimates when true values are near or below 50 — especially in the first 10 days — suggests sensitivity to recent low values.
- Model underestimates true values when the last 5 days are below 48 — fails to recognize potential rebound or reversal.
- Model shows lag in adjusting to true value spikes — typically 2–3 days delay in recognizing and responding to new highs.
- Model tends to underestimate true values when the last 30 days include multiple spikes — fails to capture cumulative momentum or volatility clustering.
